_why: Written 2026-08-18, the day the marketing site was rebuilt from a one-section stub. Holohound is pre-launch and its own privacy.html already made no_account/no_tracking/no_ads claims with no contract behind them — this backs those with evidence from the actual app repo (~/Developer/DrVanus/holohound) rather than removing the claims.

evidence: DESIGN.md's accepted decisions state the app is a cold open with no onboarding sequence: 'no splash, no carousel, no account, no ATT' — camera permission fires in context, account is never required to scan or see your own collection.
holohound/ios/project.yml declares zero third-party SPM/CocoaPods dependencies for the Holohound target — no auth SDK (Firebase Auth, Sign in with Apple wrapper, etc.) is linked.

Identity to the Hound backend (holohound-api) is an opaque, install-scoped localStorage id generated client-side (index.html 'HOUND, LIVE' block, deviceId()) — explicitly documented as 'a METERING key, not a credential'. There is no login, password or profile screen anywhere in the 13-screen prototype.

holohound/ios/project.yml lists only first-party Swift sources for the Holohound target (HolohoundApp, Haptics, Recognition, Scanner, Grading, PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy) and zero package dependencies — no analytics or attribution SDK (Firebase, Amplitude, Mixpanel, PostHog, AppsFlyer, Adjust) is linked.

Card recognition is on-device: DESIGN.md and the app's own NSCameraUsageDescription ('Recognition runs entirely on this device') describe a bundled pHash index (tools/build_phash_index.py --games pokemon,mtg, 124,248 EN paper printings: 19,502 Pokemon + 104,746 Magic, read from the HHX2 header of ios/Holohound/Resources/hhindex.bin) matched locally, with no image or video sent anywhere.

The only network calls in the prototype are to the five game catalogues — api.tcgdex.net + assets.tcgdex.net (Pokemon), api.scryfall.com (Magic), db.ygoprodeck.com (Yu-Gi-Oh!), api.lorcast.com (Lorcana), api.gcgapi.com (Gundam) — all public card/price data with no identifier attached (FEED_NAME_OF, mock-data.js) and to holohound-api for Hound chat, LIVE since 2026-08-18 (index.html 'HOUND, LIVE' block; default HOUND_API = https://holohound-api.fly.dev). That call carries an install-scoped device id and is metered per day and per IP (holohound-api/src/middleware/meter.js) — metering, not tracking: it is joined to nothing, and holohound-api stores no message content.
Same project.yml dependency list as no_tracking: no ad SDK (Google Mobile Ads/AdMob, AppLovin, Unity Ads, ironSource) is linked anywhere in the iOS shell.

DESIGN.md's paywall copy law (accepted decisions) rules out ad-supported mechanics entirely: monetisation is INTENDED to be a single subscription (Holohound Pro, $9.99/mo or $59.99/yr in the mock's PLANS block, mock-data.js:2327-2331), with 'exactly two paywall entry points' and no rewarded-ad or ad-gated surface described anywhere in the design log. NOTE, and it is why the site may not say the app is purchasable: that plan is display-only. There is no StoreKit code, no product identifier and no purchase anywhere in the holohound repo, and the app is not on the App Store.

evidence: holohound/tools/check_index_count.py re-derives it from the binary on every run
facts._why_not_19502: 19,502 is the RETIRED TOTAL and also the TRUE Pokemon subset, and a substring gate cannot tell the two apart. Forbidding it would fail an honest sentence ('19,502 Pokemon and 104,746 Magic'), and a gate that fails honest copy is a gate that gets switched off. Only figures that are false in every reading are listed.
facts._why_forbidden_shape: FORBIDDEN VALUES ARE MARKUP-COUPLED OR FULL PHRASES, NEVER BARE FRAGMENTS, AND THAT IS THIS FILE'S OWN BUG BEING FIXED. This contract is SERVED — hypersage.ai/holohound/site-audit-contract.json returns 200 — so every literal written here is published. The first version of these gates listed bare '21,775' and '10 a day', which put the retired claims back on the very origin they were removed from: a grep of the live site reported them as live again, which is exactly the trap that cost this sweep an hour. A literal that only occurs inside markup, or a phrase long enough to be unmistakable, gates the same regression without republishing the claim. Numeric drift is caught by the positive `value` arm anyway, which fails the moment the shipped number stops matching.

10
free Hound questions a day
facts._why_forbidden_shape: The number and its label are separate elements, so the only exact literal for this regression is the markup-coupled one. It is also unmistakably markup rather than a claim, which is the property this file needs. See index_card_count's note.

evidence: The five catalogues in holohound/mock-data.js FEED_NAME_OF, each of which receives the user's IP
forbidden_values: Prices shown in the app are TCGplayer market prices supplied through TCGdex
facts._why: Two live-legal-document defects, fixed 2026-08-31. (1) 'your notification choices' outlived the feature: the binary has ZERO notification capability — no UNUserNotification, no registerForRemoteNotifications, no aps-environment anywhere in the Swift or the project spec — so the policy listed a choice the user cannot make. It is the phantom-alerts claim surviving in the legal page after the landing page was cleaned, which is why a claims sweep has to cover every surface and not just the loudest one. (2) The page named TCGdex as the only recipient of card requests while four more catalogues receive the user's IP.

data_flows._why: Each game's catalogue is a separate third party receiving the user's IP and the identity of the cards they looked at. Naming one of five is a materially incomplete disclosure, and it is the shape the page had until 2026-08-31.
The only outbound flow carrying anything the user wrote.
